title: G7 SBOM for AI, minimum elements

sourceDocuments.title: Software Bill of Materials for AI - Minimum Elements
sourceDocuments.publisher: G7 Cybersecurity Working Group, published by BSI (Germany), ACN (Italy), ANSSI (France), CSE (Canada), CISA (United States), NCSC (United Kingdom), NCO (Japan)
sourceDocuments.retrievedNote: cisa.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated requests. BSI is a co-publisher and hosts the identical original.
sourceDocuments.normativeLanguageEvidence: The document states of itself: "These minimum elements are not mandatory; do not create requirements, standards, or legislation." It assigns no required, optional or recommended level to any element and uses no RFC 2119 keywords, so every element in the crosswalk is marked 'unspecified'. The loader must refuse severity 'error' on any rule citing it.

sitsOnTopOf.title: 2026 Minimum Elements for a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
sitsOnTopOf.quote: The minimum elements in an SBOM for AI are in addition to the general SBOM minimum elements.

severityModel.justification: The source assigns no conformance level to any of its 50 elements and says in terms that they are not mandatory. Every severity here is StratifyPro's judgement about what a consumer of the SBOM cannot work around, never a quotation of an obligation. Firms may override any of them.
severityModel.maxSeverityNote: normativeLanguage is false, so the loader refuses 'error' on every rule in this pack. Nothing here escalates by citing a different source: a rule that needs 'error' is making a claim this document does not support.

conformanceNote: The source specification assigns no required, optional or recommended level to any element, and uses no RFC 2119 keywords. Every element here is marked 'unspecified'. Any conformance policy is the implementer's own and should be declared as such.
coverageNote: One rule per element, 50 of 50. CycloneDX only: the crosswalk maps 44 elements into SPDX 3.0.1, and the engine reads SPDX 3 by normalising it, which the reference engine used to prove fixtures does not yet do. CycloneDX carries all 50 elements, so the element list is complete either way.
